title: Constant-factor approximation for Dasgupta’s hierarchical clustering objective
area: Approximation algorithms and hardness of approximation
formal: Do a universal constant \(C\ge 1\) and a deterministic polynomial-time algorithm exist which, for every finite undirected graph \(G=([n],E)\) with nonnegative rational edge weights w, output a rooted full binary tree T whose leaves are bijectively labeled by \([n]\) and whose cost is at most C times the minimum cost of such a tree, where \(\operatorname{cost}_{G}(T)=\sum _{\{u,v\}\in E}w_{uv}|\mathrm{L}_{T}\)(\(lca_{T}(u,v)\))|?
definitions: Here \(n\ge 2\). The least common ancestor \(lca_{T}(u,v)\) is the lowest common ancestor of the leaves u and v. \(\mathrm{L}_{T}(z)\) is the set of leaves below node z, including a leaf itself. Every internal node has exactly two children. Weights are encoded by binary integer numerators and positive denominators; running time is polynomial in the total explicit input bit length. If all weights vanish, every tree has zero cost. The output tree is explicit. No auxiliary distance, planted model or triplet-query oracle is given.

context_blocks.text: Dasgupta’s objective makes hierarchical clustering a single optimization problem: heavily connected items pay more when they are separated high in the hierarchy. This gives a mathematically specified approximation question on arbitrary similarity graphs.

Known general guarantees and conditional hardness leave a substantial gap. The Small-Set Expansion hypothesis rules out constant-factor approximation, but that is a conditional barrier rather than an unconditional resolution. Constant guarantees with extra comparison oracles concern a different input model.

why: The principal approximation barrier for a foundational objective in hierarchical clustering, with links to graph partitioning and metric optimization.
answer_criterion: Prove the stated proposition or its logical negation, preserving the quantifiers, model and guarantees. Conditional results settle only their conditional claims. Benchmark acceptance requires a complete proof-assistant-checked proof of the full target.
